messages:
mari: Heads-up, CI blocked on feature/regen-cleanup. typegen produced a regen diff that only reorders changelog arrays and tweaks README example indentation. semver guard is treating it as a breaking change and blocking publish.

oz: Seen it. The regendiff is docs-only but we currently fail CI on any regen mismatch. Which part of the generator touched ordering?

regen-bot: pipeline: typegen #5142 failed (exit 1). Artifact: /artifacts/typegen/2967890123/regendiff.log

kai: Paste from regendiff: ```diff
-  - changelog: ["alpha", "beta"]
+  - changelog: ["beta", "alpha"]
```

priya: Also noticed generated READMEs show different 'retry' defaults between python and node after regen (3 vs 2), which causes sampleapp smoke tests to flip. That makes it a DX parity issue, not just docs.

mari: Two parallel fixes: (1) short-term: change semver guard to WARN for docs-only diffs (changelogs, README examples, docs/*) so releases aren't blocked but reviewers still see a warning; (2) long-term: fix generator determinism and add idempotence CI.

oz: For (2) propose adding an idempotence job that runs regen twice for PRs touching openapi/ or generator/ and fails if git is dirty. Also add a small parity check that diffs auth/retry blocks across SDK READMEs and fails DX tests if they disagree.

kai: I'll open a PR to canonicalize $ref traversal order and normalize arrays in changelog metadata. That should reduce the noise.

priya: I'll implement the README parity check in sampleapp CI and gate the regen-idempotence job to generator/spec PRs to save minutes.

mari: Filing an incident to unstick the release: https://redwood-internal/ops/INC-2051-regen-doc-noise. I'll manually unblock this publish once the semver-guard -> WARN patch is merged.

oz: Also add a unit test that runs regen twice on an anyOf-heavy schema and asserts idempotence. Catches this earlier.

kai: Will do. Targeting both patches today so we don't block more releases.

mari: Thanks all. Small follow-up: if parity check flags README retry mismatch, fail DX-check but don't auto-block release until a human reviews. We want signal, not noise.

priya: Agreed. I'll surface it to #devex with a short summary and link back to the PRs.

oz: Nice. :thumbsup:
